overall_summary: Core niche content ('self respect' digital detachment) yielded low double-digit views, but family-centric emotional shorts (Maa, Papa) dramatically outperformed them organically (up to 215 views). The audience responds strongly to raw emotional relational ties rather than purely micro-digital breakup tropes, though digital self-respect has a loyal baseline. We should lean into the higher-performing emotional relational space while retaining the core brand identity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos about Mother (OfHrAp3r1G8) and Father (v8krtdmxbPs) got 215 and 122 views respectively, significantly outperforming digital breakup clips.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate broader emotional family/relationship bonds into the content mix to scale reach.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos dealing with direct actions like clearing chat lists or removing pins (e.g., Y4finYMxnIU, rwOUYo_hayQ) performed relatively stable around 32-41 views.
winning_patterns.action: Keep digital detachment hooks ultra-specific and grounded in everyday phone habits.

weak_patterns.pattern: Overly abstract or niche digital micro-actions
weak_patterns.evidence: Recent niche experiments like unlinking streaming profiles or removing widgets (e.g., cuKSS0gHyt0, 6KVEZc22kS8) dropped to 0-1 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid hyper-niche app features that lack universal emotional relatability.
